name.value: Widzin Kwah Canyon House Museum (Widzin Kwah Diyik Be Yikh)

description.value: The Widzin Kwah Canyon House Museum sits above the famous Widzin Kwah (Bulkley River) Canyon, where visitors can watch traditional Witsuwit'en fishermen at work below. The museum holds artifacts and recently excavated stone tools carbon-dated back 6,000 years from the ground on which it stands, and offers professionally guided 45-minute cultural tours covering Witsuwit'en clan history, archaeology, and traditional fishing technologies. Authentic locally made moccasins, beaded jewelry, and native art are available for purchase on site.

raw_osm.name: Widzin Kwah Canyon House Museum (Widzin Kwah Diyik Be Yikh)

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content from witset.ca/museum confirmed the museum is a genuine, publicly accessible cultural attraction operated by Witset First Nation at the Widzin Kwah (Bulkley River) Canyon. Phone (250) 847-2133 and address #3-205 Beaver Rd are corroborated on both the museum page footer and the contact subpage, though this appears to be the Band Office address rather than the museum's canyon-side location. No bike parking, washrooms, or cycling-specific amenities are mentioned anywhere on the website or in OSM tags; only confectionary items and complimentary coffee are noted as food/beverage offerings.
concerns: Address in OSM is empty; the address used (#3-205 Beaver Rd) is the Witset Band Office, not the museum's physical canyon-side location — the actual museum address should be verified.
Website copyright reads ©2019, suggesting the site may not have been updated recently; hours and seasonal operation details should be confirmed for the current season.
Museum is seasonally operated (May to September per website); directory listing should reflect this to avoid off-season visits.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, publicly accessible indigenous cultural attraction at a world-renowned fishing canyon on a touring route through BC's North; the guided tours and historic artifacts make it a worthwhile destination stop for cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: The museum is operated by Witset First Nation as part of a broader Witsuwit'en cultural tourism program that also includes a separate canyon tour. The Witset Canyon Path Project (a trail construction initiative) is a related but distinct community project.

Café or food on site.detail: Website notes 'a limited number of confectionary items' for sale and a 'complimentary cup of coffee' offered to visitors at the museum
